questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding connective tissue?

options.text: Fat storing adipose tissue is found above the skin
Areolar connective tissue is found between the skin and muscle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat storing adipose tissue is found above the skin**__.

__
 
• **Adipose tissue**, commonly referred to as fat tissue, is primarily located beneath the skin (subcutaneous layer), around internal organs, and in certain areas of the body like the abdomen and thighs.
 
• It serves as **energy storage**, insulation to maintain body temperature, and cushioning to protect vital organs.
 
• The statement that fat-storing adipose tissue is found above the skin is incorrect, as adipose tissue is specifically located **beneath the skin** (subcutaneous layer) rather than above it.
 
• Adipose tissue is classified into two types: **white adipose tissue (WAT)**, which stores energy and insulates the body, and **brown adipose tissue (BAT)**, which generates heat through thermogenesis.
 
• The primary function of adipose tissue is to store triglycerides and release them when the body requires energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ligaments connect bone to bone:**
 
 
• Ligaments are tough, fibrous connective tissues that connect bones to other bones, providing stability to joints.
 
• They are primarily made of collagen fibers, giving them strength and flexibility.
 
• Ligaments prevent excessive movement and dislocation of joints, ensuring proper alignment during physical activity.
 
• Examples include the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in the knee and the ulnar collateral ligament in the elbow.
 
 
 
• **Areolar connective tissue is found between the skin and muscle:**
 
 
• Areolar connective tissue is a loose connective tissue that fills the space between organs and connects the skin to underlying muscles.
 
• It contains fibroblasts, collagen, and elastic fibers, allowing flexibility and support.
 
• Areolar tissue plays a significant role in providing a medium for nutrient and waste exchange between blood vessels and cells.
 
• It also houses immune cells that help defend the body against pathogens in the surrounding tissues.
 
 
 
• **Tendons connect muscle to bone:**
 
 
• Tendons are strong, fibrous connective tissues that attach muscles to bones, enabling movement of the skeleton.
 
• They are composed of dense regular connective tissue with parallel collagen fibers, allowing them to withstand tension during muscle contraction.
 
• Examples include the Achilles tendon, which connects the calf muscles to the heel bone.
 
• Tendons work in coordination with muscles to ensure efficient movement and force transmission during physical activities.

questions.question: Which of the following glands secretes growth hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pituitary gland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pituitary gland, often referred to as the "master gland," is responsible for secreting growth hormone (GH), also known as somatotropin.
 
• Growth hormone plays a critical role in stimulating growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration in humans and animals.
 
• It is secreted by the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, which is located at the base of the brain, beneath the hypothalamus.
 
• This hormone is particularly active during childhood and adolescence, promoting the growth of bones and tissues.
 
• The secretion of growth hormone is regulated by two hypothalamic hormones: growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) and somatostatin (growth hormone-inhibiting hormone).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Testes:**
 
 
• The testes are male reproductive glands responsible for producing sperm and the male hormone testosterone.
 
• Testosterone plays a key role in the development of male secondary sexual characteristics such as facial hair growth, deepening of the voice, and muscle growth.
 
• The testes do not secrete growth hormone; their primary function is related to reproduction and male hormonal regulation.
 
 
 
• **Ovaries:**
 
 
• The ovaries are female reproductive glands that produce eggs (ova) and secrete hormones such as estrogen and progesterone.
 
• These hormones regulate the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and the development of female secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• Like the testes, the ovaries are not involved in the secretion of growth hormone.
 
 
 
• **Thyroid gland:**
 
 
• The thyroid gland is located in the neck and produces hormones such as thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
 
• These hormones regulate metabolism, energy production, and overall growth and development, but they do not directly secrete growth hormone.
 
• The thyroid gland works in coordination with the pituitary gland to regulate growth and metabolic functions.
 
 
 
• **Growth hormone and its importance:**
 
 
• Growth hormone deficiency can lead to growth-related disorders such as dwarfism in children.
 
• Excessive secretion of growth hormone can result in gigantism (in children) or acromegaly (in adults).
 
• Therapeutically, growth hormone is used to treat growth disorders and hormonal deficiencies in both children and adults.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A car approaching a school zone slows down from 36 m/s to 9 m/s with constant acceleration -3 m/s². How much time is car required to slow down to final velocity?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**9 seconds**__

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The relation between velocity and time during uniformly accelerated, straight-line motion is a simple one. The longer the acceleration, the greater the velocity change. Change in velocity when the acceleration is constant is directly proportional to the time.

**a = ∆v/∆t **

Expand ∆v to v - u

**and condense ∆t to t**

**a = (v − u)/t **

Then,

solve for v as a function of t.

**v = u + at **

u = Initial Velocity

v = Final Velocity

a = Acceleration

t = Time

**Calculations:**__

**Given that, **

The initial velocity** (u) = 36 m/s **

The final velocity** (v) = 9 m/s **

Acceleration** (a) = -3 m/s²,**

Find time t =?

To find the value of t, we use 1st euation of motion,

***v = u + at ***

v - u = at

**(v - u)/a = t**

Now, put all values in the above equation,

t = (9-36)/(-3)

t = (-27)/(-3)

**t = 9 seconds**

The car required** 9 seconds** to slow down to their final velocity.

__
 
• **Plasma's function** is to** transport nutrients, hormones, and proteins** throughout the body.
 
• It also transports **waste products of cell metabolism **from different tissues to the organs that detoxify and/or excrete them.
 
• Plasma is** 90% water,** with the remaining** 10% **consisting of ions, proteins, dissolved gases, nutritional molecules, and wastes.
 
• Plasma proteins are of **three different types**: **albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen.**
 
• **Albumin__:**
 __
 
• Albumin aids in the maintenance of the **blood's colloid osmotic pressure.**
 
• It is the **smallest **of the plasma proteins, but it accounts for the **majority of the total.**
 
• The blood's colloid osmotic pressure is critical for maintaining a** balance between the water inside the blood and the water** in the tissue fluid surrounding the cells.
 
• When **plasma proteins are lacking,** the water in the plasma leaks into the area around the blood vessels, causing **interstitial edema,** which is a symptom of liver illness, kidney disease, and malnutrition, among other things.
 
• Albumin also aids in the** transfer of a variety of molecules**, including **medicines, hormones, and fatty acids.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Insulin__:**
 
 
• Insulin is a hormone created by your** pancreas** that controls the** amount of glucose** in your bloodstream at any given moment.

questions.question: A thief noticing a policeman from a distance of 500 metres starts running at a speed of 8 km/h. The policeman chased him with a speed of 11 km/h. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught? (Rounded off to two decimal places, if required)

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **time** is constant, **distance** is directly proportional to **speed**.

Speed Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Distance Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Difference in distance ratio parts = 11 − 8 = 3 units → 500 m

Distance run by thief = (8 ÷ 3) × 500 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:** Relative Speed = Vₚ − Vₜ | Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed | Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62e5ee22ec334ba23d8315cbdeb4a7790c25d9d6780d1185848ca8d7d65178c0.png]

⇒ 3 km/h in m/s = 3 × (5/18) = 5/6 m/s

⇒ Time to catch = Initial distance ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ (5/6) = (500 × 6) ÷ 5 = 600 seconds

⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 8 × (5/18) = 20/9 m/s

⇒ Distance run by thief = Speed × Time = (20/9) × 600

⇒ Distance = 12000 ÷ 9 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

questions.question: From the top of a tree 7 m high, the angle of elevation of a tower is 30°. If the tower is 47 m high, how far away from the tower is the tree positioned?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **height difference** between the **tower** and the **tree** is 47 − 7 = 40 m.

In a 30°−60°−90° right triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to the angles is 1 : √3 : 2.

The side opposite to 30° represents the **height difference** = 1 unit = 40 m.

The side opposite to 60° represents the **horizontal distance** = √3 units = 40√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 40√3 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of the **tree** = 7 m, Height of the **tower** = 47 m, **Angle of elevation** = 30°.

**Formula:** tan θ = Opposite / Adjacent

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aecf876ffdfcaafa19a68f0f10c506e503d043dfa8f0510cda0529f2a2c5573a.png] 

⇒ Height of tower above the tree level = 47 m − 7 m = 40 m.

⇒ Let the distance between the tree and the tower be **d**.

⇒ In the right-angled triangle formed at the top:

⇒ tan 30° = 40 / d

⇒ 1 / √3 = 40 / d

⇒ d = 40 × √3

⇒ d = 40√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 40√3 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed **above** the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios for 30°

For a 30° angle: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, and **tan 30° = 1/√3**.

Relation between Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation from point A to point B is always **equal** to the angle of depression from point B to point A due to alternate interior angles.</p

questions.question: A boatman can row his boat in still water at a speed of 9 km/h. He can also row 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 9 hours. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Speed of Boat (u)** = 9 km/h and **Speed of Stream** = v km/h.

Downstream Speed (D) = 9 + v and Upstream Speed (U) = 9 − v.

Using 44/D + 35/U = 9: By **Hit and Trial**, if v = 2, D = 11 and U = 7.

⇒ 44/11 + 35/7 = 4 + 5 = 9 hours (Satisfied).

New Time = 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba671d428e36482b4e513a5e5118e44dace6be2f2170fad78993a404c70d6cc5.png] 

**Given:** Speed of boat in still water (u) = 9 km/h. Total time for 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream = 9 hours.

**Formula:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed; Downstream Speed (D) = u + v; Upstream Speed (U) = u − v.

⇒ 44/(9 + v) + 35/(9 − v) = 9

⇒ 44(9 − v) + 35(9 + v) = 9(81 − v²)

⇒ 396 − 44v + 315 + 35v = 729 − 9v²

⇒ 711 − 9v = 729 − 9v²

⇒ 9v² − 9v − 18 = 0 ⇒ v² − v − 2 = 0

⇒ (v − 2)(v + 1) = 0 ⇒ v = 2 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

⇒ Downstream Speed = 9 + 2 = 11 km/h; Upstream Speed = 9 − 2 = 7 km/h.

⇒ Required Time = 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat and Stream

Speed of boat in still water (u) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

Speed of stream (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed in Boats

Average speed for a round trip = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still water speed.</p

questions.question: If (x-(1)/(x-2))=7, then the value of (x - 2)³ - (1)/((x-2)³) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given equation: x − 1/(x − 2) = 7

Subtract **2** from both sides: (x − 2) − 1/(x − 2) = 5

Let (x − 2) = k. Then k − 1/k = 5.

The required value is k³ − 1/k³ = k³ + 3k

Shortcut: 5³ + 3 × 5 = 125 + 15 = 140

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x − 1/(x − 2) = 7

**Formula Used:** (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f6798cca3eb1783075008daf85a0102b46a4d99409e17e5d0beb9c210b3a203.png] 

⇒ Let m = (x − 2)

⇒ x = m + 2

⇒ (m + 2) − 1/m = 7

⇒ m − 1/m = 7 − 2 = 5

⇒ Cubing both sides: (m − 1/m)³ = 5³

⇒ m³ − 1/m³ − 3 × m × (1/m) × (m − 1/m) = 125

⇒ m³ − 1/m³ − 3(5) = 125

⇒ m³ − 1/m³ = 125 + 15

⇒ (x − 2)³ − 1/(x − 2)³ = 140

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Identity (Plus)

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Square Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2. If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Power 4 Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.</p

questions.question: A train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the same direction as that of the train in (25)/(2) sec and the same train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the opposite direction as that of the train in (25)/(3) sec. Find the length of the train. (in m)

questions.question: sqrt{sec²theta~+~cosec²theta}~times~sqrt{tan²theta~-~sin²theta}~=~?

__Shortcut Trick__

Apply **trigonometric properties**: √(sec²θ + cosec²θ) = secθ × cosecθ.

Apply property: √(tan²θ − sin²θ) = tanθ × sinθ.

Multiply: (secθ × cosecθ) × (tanθ × sinθ) = (1/cosθ × 1/sinθ) × (sinθ/cosθ × sinθ).

Simplify: (1/cosθ) × (sinθ/cosθ) = sinθ/cos²θ = sinθ × sec²θ.

**∴ The correct answer is sinθ × sec²θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √(sec²θ + cosec²θ) × √(tan²θ − sin²θ)

**Formula Used:** sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, secθ = 1/cosθ, cosecθ = 1/sinθ, tanθ = sinθ/cosθ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1b89065126a6f80f8e5b2474ab4106da1c0afee9192aeed09be8ad986170af3.png] 

⇒ Term 1 = √(1/cos²θ + 1/sin²θ) = √((sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sin²θcos²θ))

⇒ Term 1 = √(1 / (sin²θcos²θ)) = 1 / (sinθcosθ)

⇒ Term 2 = √((sin²θ / cos²θ) − sin²θ) = √(sin²θ (1/cos²θ − 1))

⇒ Term 2 = √(sin²θ × tan²θ) = sinθtanθ = sin²θ / cosθ

⇒ Product = [1 / (sinθcosθ)] × [sin²θ / cosθ]

⇒ Product = sinθ / cos²θ = sinθ × sec²θ

**∴ The correct answer is sinθ × sec²θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Special Product Identities

For any angle θ, the sum of squares of reciprocal functions often converts to a product: sec²θ + cosec²θ = sec²θ × cosec²θ.

Tangent-Sin Relationship

The difference between tangent squared and sine squared is equal to their product: tan²θ − sin²θ = tan²θ × sin²θ.

Fundamental Pythagorean Identity

questions.question: X and Y invest Rs. 5200 and Rs. 6200 respectively in a business. If X doubles his capital after 6 months. In what ratio should X and Y divide that year's profit ?

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 40% on his articles and still makes a profit of 20%. How much cost price does a shopkeeper pay for an article whose marked price is ₹2,400?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**.

Ratio formula: **CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)**.

CP ÷ 2,400 = (100 − 40) ÷ (100 + 20) = 60 ÷ 120 = 1 ÷ 2.

2 units = 2,400 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** MP = ₹2,400, Discount = 40%, Profit = 20%.
**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100 | CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + P%).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfd4bad5fab339cfa3e89343db57face4aababf1ee2aa7efdceaff3660241a76.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 2,400 × (100 − 40) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 2,400 × 60 ÷ 100 = ₹1,440

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP = 1,440 × 100 ÷ 120 = 12 × 100 = ₹1,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Marked Price is the price printed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

CP-MP Relation

The ratio CP:MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%) is very useful for competitive exams to save time when **Profit** and **Discount** are both provided.

questions.question: A chord 21 cm long is drawn in a circle of diameter 25 cm. The perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Radius** (r) = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm

Half of the **chord** (a) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

Using the **Pythagorean relation** for the **perpendicular distance** (d):

⇒ d = √(r² − a²)

⇒ d = √(12.5² − 10.5²)

⇒ d = √((12.5 − 10.5) × (12.5 + 10.5)) = √(2 × 23) = √46 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of the circle = 25 cm

Length of the **chord** = 21 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Radius** (r) = **Diameter** ÷ 2

The **perpendicular** drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

In a **right-angled triangle**, by **Pythagoras theorem**: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a15536eb57cbd2165e9577777654cfdc2398472e789e84633dfca39f2545c9aa.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let O be the centre of the circle and AC be the chord of length 21 cm.

Let OM be the perpendicular from the centre O to the chord AC.

⇒ **Radius** of the circle (OA) = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm

⇒ Since OM is perpendicular to AC, it bisects AC.

⇒ AM = MC = AC ÷ 2 = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

In **right-angled triangle** OMA, by **Pythagoras theorem**:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 12.5² = OM² + 10.5²

⇒ 156.25 = OM² + 110.25

⇒ OM² = 156.25 − 110.25

⇒ OM² = 46

⇒ OM = √46 cm

**Option Evaluation:**

Option (1) √41 is incorrect because 12.5² − 10.5² = 46, not 41.

Option (2) √23 is incorrect because the square of the distance is 46, not 23.

Option (3) √56 is incorrect because 156.25 − 110.25 = 46, not 56.

Option (4) √46 is correct as it perfectly satisfies the Pythagorean relation OM = √46 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is √46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Height².

Chord Length Formula

The length of a chord can be calculated as 2 × √(r² − d²), where r is the radius and d is the perpendicular distance from the centre.</p

questions.question: The area enclosed between the circumferences of two concentric circles is 16π cm2 and their radii are in the ratio 5 ∶ 3. What is the area of the outer circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of radii (R : r) = 5 : 3

Ratio of areas (R² : r²) = 5² : 3² = 25 : 9

Difference in area units = 25 − 9 = 16 units

Given, 16 units = 16π cm² ⇒ 1 unit = π cm²

Area of outer circle = 25 units = 25 × π = 25π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 25π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area between circles = 16π cm²

Ratio of radii R : r = 5 : 3

**Formula Used:**

Area of circle = πr²

Area of ring = π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9ada9308556c9bccdca62097881b54a5b002eafa6d692dc840c80f91c4d8bb1.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the radii be 5x and 3x.

⇒ π[(5x)² − (3x)²] = 16π

⇒ 25x² − 9x² = 16

⇒ 16x² = 16

⇒ x² = 1

⇒ x = 1

⇒ Outer radius (R) = 5 × 1 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of outer circle = π × (5)²

⇒ Area = 25π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 25π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentric Circles

Circles having the same center but different radii are called concentric circles. The region between them is called an annulus or ring.

Circumference Difference

The difference between the circumferences of two concentric circles is given by 2π(R − r), which is also 2π times the width of the ring.

Area Scaling Rule

If the radii of two circles are in the ratio a : b, then their areas are in the ratio a² : b².</p

questions.question: For the quadratic equation x² + bx + c = 0, If the sum of roots is -8 and product of the two roots is 16, then find the value of (b + c).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **quadratic equation** x² + bx + c = 0, the value **b = −(Sum of roots)** and **c = Product of roots**.

Given **Sum** = −8 and **Product** = 16.

⇒ **b** = −(−8) = 8 and **c** = 16.

⇒ Required value **(b + c)** = 8 + 16 = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Sum of roots** (α + β) = −8 and **Product of roots** (αβ) = 16.

**Formula Used:** A **quadratic equation** with roots α and β is given by x² − (α + β)x + (αβ) = 0.

⇒ x² − (−8)x + 16 = 0

⇒ x² + 8x + 16 = 0

⇒ Comparing this with the given equation x² + bx + c = 0:

⇒ **b** = 8 and **c** = 16

⇒ Calculation for (b + c): 8 + 16 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Roots and Coefficients

For a general quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **sum of roots** is −b/a and the **product of roots** is c/a.

Nature of Roots

The nature is determined by the **Discriminant** D = b² − 4ac. If D = 0, as in this case (8² − 4×1×16 = 0), the roots are **real and equal**.

Standard Form of Quadratic Equation

Any quadratic equation can be represented as x² − (Sum of roots)x + (Product of roots) = 0 when the coefficient of x² is 1.</p

questions.question: In a class of 130 students, a class test for two subjects Physics and Chemistry was conducted. (x + 40) students passed in Physics and (x + 30) students passed in chemistry and no student failed in both subjects. If 60 students passed in both subject, then, what is the number of students passed in only physics?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total students = P + C − Both

130 = (x + 40) + (x + 30) − 60

130 = 2x + 10 ⇒ 2x = 120 ⇒ x = 60

Only Physics = (x + 40) − 60 = 100 − 60 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34d7011c2928759fc39cf668acf8456eed2414a16fded5b62e4d241897cf78e6.png] 

**Given:**

Total students = 130

Passed in **Physics** = x + 40

Passed in **Chemistry** = x + 30

Passed in **Both subjects** = 60

**Formula Used:** n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

⇒ 130 = (x + 40) + (x + 30) − 60

⇒ 130 = 2x + 70 − 60

⇒ 130 = 2x + 10

⇒ 2x = 120

⇒ x = 60

⇒ Students passed in **Physics** = 60 + 40 = 100

⇒ Students passed in **Only Physics** = Total Physics − Both

⇒ Students passed in **Only Physics** = 100 − 60 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Venn Diagram for Two Sets

For two sets A and B, the number of elements in **exactly one set** is given by [n(A) + n(B) − 2×n(A ∩ B)].

Set Theory Basics

Total = n(Only A) + n(Only B) + n(Both) + n(None). If no one fails, n(None) = 0.</p

questions.question: If (x + y) : (y + z) : (z + x) = 11 : 13 : 16, and x + y + z = 200, then find the value of z.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ratio parts = 11 + 13 + 16 = 40 units

This sum represents 2 × (x + y + z) = 2 × 200 = 400

1 unit = 400 ÷ 40 = 10

Value of (x + y) = 11 units = 11 × 10 = 110

Value of z = (x + y + z) − (x + y) = 200 − 110 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(x + y) : (y + z) : (z + x) = 11 : 13 : 16

Total sum x + y + z = 200

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33730484ad4074e2195338e7e2b95614870f61ba1e410f1b3d3ac6e68a1d51e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let (x + y) = 11k, (y + z) = 13k, and (z + x) = 16k

⇒ (x + y) + (y + z) + (z + x) = 11k + 13k + 16k

⇒ 2(x + y + z) = 40k

⇒ 2(200) = 40k

⇒ 400 = 40k

⇒ k = 400 ÷ 40 = 10

⇒ x + y = 11k = 11 × 10 = 110

⇒ z = (x + y + z) − (x + y)

⇒ z = 200 − 110 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Sum Property

When cyclic sums like (a+b), (b+c), and (c+a) are given in a ratio, the sum of the ratio parts always equals 2 × (a+b+c).

Finding Individual Variables

To find variable z, subtract the pair (x + y) from the total (x + y + z). Similarly, x = Total − (y + z) and y = Total − (z + x).

Ratio Constant (k)

The constant k is the proportionality factor that converts ratio units into actual numerical values based on the given constraints.</p

questions.question: Simple interest and compound interest (compounding annually) on a principal at a certain rate of interest for 2 years is Rs. 12000 and Rs. 14400 respectively. What is the principal?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a 2-year period, **Principal (P)** can be calculated using the direct formula:

**P = (SI²) ÷ [4 × (CI − SI)]**

Given: **SI = ₹12,000** and **CI = ₹14,400**

⇒ P = (12,000 × 12,000) ÷ [4 × (14,400 − 12,000)]

⇒ P = 144,000,000 ÷ 9,600 = **₹15,000**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (**SI**) for 2 years = **₹12,000**

Compound Interest (**CI**) for 2 years = **₹14,400**

**Formula Used:**

1. **SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100**

2. Difference (**D**) for 2 years = **CI − SI**

3. Rate (**R**) = (**D** ÷ **SI for 1 year**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bcf64456b4a384711674e7540fc02e49b5b7315b7d08b234aa7c368e302a81f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **SI for 1 year** = 12,000 ÷ 2 = **₹6,000**

⇒ Difference (**D**) = 14,400 − 12,000 = **₹2,400**

⇒ This difference is the **interest** on the first year's interest (₹6,000).

⇒ Rate of Interest (**R**) = (2,400 ÷ 6,000) × 100 = **40%**

⇒ Now, using 1st year SI to find Principal (**P**):

⇒ 6,000 = (P × 40 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (6,000 × 100) ÷ 40

⇒ **P = ₹15,000**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

SI and CI for 1st Year

When the interest is **compounded annually**, the simple interest and compound interest for the **first year** are always equal.

Difference Formula for 2 Years

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years is given by: **D = P × (R/100)²**.

Difference Formula for 3 Years

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 3 years is given by: **D = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100)**.

questions.question: Three-fifths of my current age is the same as five-sixths of that of one of my cousins’. My age ten years ago will be his age four years hence. My current age is ______ years.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **My age** (M) to **Cousin's age** (C) → M × (3/5) = C × (5/6) ⇒ M : C = 25 : 18.

The difference between ages remains **constant**; here M − 10 = C + 4 ⇒ M − C = 14 years.

In ratio, difference = 25 − 18 = 7 units.

7 units = 14 years ⇒ 1 unit = 2 years.

**My current age** = 25 units × 2 = 50 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(3/5) × **Current Age** (M) = (5/6) × **Cousin's Age** (C)

M − 10 = C + 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f1fdab5fe6a4d3de31fa3985e6f3fcbcf7f17ea0601bdc7292e97a8b80474e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (3/5)M = (5/6)C

⇒ 18M = 25C ⇒ M = 25C/18

⇒ From the second condition: M − C = 10 + 4

⇒ M − C = 14

⇒ (25C/18) − C = 14

⇒ (25C − 18C) / 18 = 14

⇒ 7C / 18 = 14

⇒ C = (14 × 18) ÷ 7 = 36 years

⇒ M = 36 + 14 = 50 years

**∴ The correct answer is 50 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Age Ratio Rule

If the ratio of ages of two persons is a:b and the **difference** between their ages is D, then their actual ages are [a ÷ (a−b)] × D and [b ÷ (a−b)] × D.

Time Shift Property

The **age difference** between two individuals always remains **constant**, whether calculated for years ago or years hence.

Linear Equation Formulation

For 'n' years ago, subtract n (x − n) and for 'n' years hence, add n (x + n) to the **current age**.</p

questions.question: If A is 25% less than B, then what will be the value of (2B - A)/A ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume **B** = 100.

Since **A** is 25% less than **B**, **A** = 100 − 25 = 75.

Ratio **B : A** = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3.

Substitute **B** = 4 and **A** = 3 in the expression (2B − A)/A.

Value = (2 × 4 − 3) ÷ 3 = (8 − 3) ÷ 3 = 5/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25473de15e885d1a9980c60f8c389c41612bdc33b048533af90c8c127d78c49b.png] 

**Given:**

**A** = **B** − 25% of **B**

**Formula Used:**

Value = (2B − A) / A

**Calculations:**

⇒ **A** = **B** × (1 − 25/100) = **B** × (75/100)

⇒ **A** = 3**B**/4

⇒ 4**A** = 3**B** → **B** = 4**A**/3

⇒ Required value = (2(4**A**/3) − **A**) / **A**

⇒ Required value = ((8**A**/3) − **A**) / **A**

⇒ Required value = ((8**A** − 3**A**) / 3) / **A**

⇒ Required value = (5**A** / 3) / **A** = 5/3

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Base

If **x** is **r%** less than **y**, then **x** = **y** × (100 − **r**)/100. Conversely, **y** is [**r**/(100 − **r**)] × 100% more than **x**.

Fraction Equivalents

25% = 1/4. If a value is 25% less, the multiplier is (1 − 1/4) = 3/4. If 25% more, the multiplier is (1 + 1/4) = 5/4.</p

questions.question: The mode and the mean of a grouped data are 27.5 and 28.5 respectively. Find the median, correct to two places of decimal, using empirical relation.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Empirical Relation** between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**.

Substitute the values: 3 × **Median** = 27.5 + (2 × 28.5)

3 × **Median** = 27.5 + 57 = 84.5

**Median** = 84.5 ÷ 3 ≈ 28.17

**∴ The correct answer is 28.17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mode** = 27.5, **Mean** = 28.5

**Formula Used:** **Mode** = 3(**Median**) − 2(**Mean**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38b4ddb7b12c0ce733fd15becba936940f547840924834d67581c3935747499c.png] 

⇒ 27.5 = 3 × **Median** − 2 × 28.5

⇒ 27.5 = 3 × **Median** − 57

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 27.5 + 57

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 84.5

⇒ **Median** = 84.5 ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = 28.166666...

⇒ **Median** ≈ 28.17

**∴ The correct answer is 28.17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode** = 3 **Median** − 2 **Mean**, also known as **Karl Pearson's** formula.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **Symmetric Distribution**, the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Direction

If Mean > Median > Mode, the distribution is **Positively Skewed**. If Mode > Median > Mean, it is **Negatively Skewed**.

questions.question: A, B and C can alone complete a work in 15, 12, and 18 days, respectively. B and C started the work and after working 6 days, B left and A joined. In how many days was the total work completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Total Work = **LCM** of (15, 12, 18) = 180 units.

Efficiencies: A = 12, B = 15, C = 10.

Work done by B + C in 6 days = (15 + 10) × 6 = 150 units.

Remaining work = 180 − 150 = 30 units.

Time taken by A + C = 30 ÷ (12 + 10) = 30/22 = 15/11 days.

Total Time = 6 + 15/11 = 81/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 81/11 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by A = 15 days, B = 12 days, C = 18 days.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time; Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 A 15 180 12
 B 12 15
 C 18 10
⇒ Work done by **B and C** in first 6 days = (Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C) × 6

⇒ Work done = (15 + 10) × 6 = 25 × 6 = 150 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = 180 − 150 = 30 units

⇒ Now B leaves and A joins C. Combined efficiency of **A and C** = 12 + 10 = 22

⇒ Time taken by A and C to finish remaining work = 30 ÷ 22 = 15/11 days

⇒ **Total days** taken for the work = Initial 6 days + 15/11 days

⇒ Total days = (66 + 15) ÷ 11 = 81/11 days

**∴ The correct answer is 81/11 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Relation

The total work is always considered as the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual days to simplify calculations into integers.

Efficiency Concept

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If A is twice as efficient as B, A will take half the time taken by B to complete the same work.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the **actual work done** by each person, which is the product of their efficiency and the number of days they worked.</p

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is twice its breadth. If its length is decreased by 4 cm and breadth is increased by 4 cm, the area of the rectangle increases by 52 cm². The length of the rectangle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **breadth** be x, then **length** is 2x.

New Area − Old Area = 52

(2x − 4)(x + 4) − 2x² = 52

2x² + 8x − 4x − 16 − 2x² = 52 ⇒ 4x = 68 ⇒ x = 17 cm.

**Length** = 2 × 17 = 34 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length (L)** = 2 × **Breadth (B)**

New length = L − 4

New breadth = B + 4

questions.question: Which one of the following writs can be issued by a High Court to secure the liberty of an individual?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Habeas Corpus**__.

__
 
• A writ means a written command in the** name of the court. **
 
• **It is a legal document** that is issued by a **Court that orders a person or entity to perform a particular act or to stop performing a specific deed.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Article 32 of the Indian Constitution makes **deals with the law of issuing the writs by the **Supreme Court.**
 
• **Article 226** of the Indian Constitution deals with the law of issuing the writs by the **High court**.
 
• In India, **only 'prerogative writs' are issued which** are issued under different circumstances.
 
• **Prerogative writs **are of five kinds:

 
• Habeas corpus
 
• Quo warranto
 
• Mandamus
 
• Prohibition
 
• **Certiorari**

 
• **Habeas Corpus** writ is issued for securing the liberty of an individual.
 
• It is a writ requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
 
• It aims to ensure that a **fast judicial review is provided in case** of unlawful **detention hampering the liberty or freedom of the prisoner.**
